title: Transport of counit mates along compatible left-adjoint isomorphisms
statement: Let C,D,C′,D′ be categories, with adjunctions aO:LO⊣RO and aC:LC⊣RC between C,D and bO:LO′⊣RO′ and bC:LC′⊣RC′ between C′,D′ [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. Let Q:C→C′ and T:D→D′, tA:LO≅LC, tB:LO′≅LC′, qO:LO⋙T≅Q⋙LO′ and qC:LC⋙T≅Q⋙LC′. Fix K∈D, K′∈D′ and η:T(K)→K′. Suppose maps uO:Q(RO(K))→RO′(K′) and uC:Q(RC(K))→RC′(K′) satisfy LO′(uO)≫ε_bO=qO⁻¹_RO(K)≫T(ε_aO,K)≫η and LC′(uC)≫ε_bC=qC⁻¹_RC(K)≫T(ε_aC,K)≫η. Suppose also T(tA_RO(K))≫qC_RO(K)=qO_RO(K)≫tB_Q(RO(K)). Then there exist object isomorphisms eA:RO(K)≅RC(K) and eB:RO′(K′)≅RC′(K′) such that Q(eA)≫uC=uO≫eB. Here the adjunction transpose of x:F(X)→Y is the actual map η_X≫G(x):X→G(Y).

source.place: paragraph 3, transposition and compatibility with the specified counit

proof.text: Transport aO and bO across tA and tB and apply uniqueness of right adjoints against aC and bC. Evaluate the resulting natural isomorphisms at K and K′; their counit equations are the right-adjoint uniqueness counit formulas.

Invert the coefficient square using both natural isomorphisms. Transpose the required equality under bC. Naturality moves eA and tB past qC and uO, respectively, and substitution of the two assumed counit equations leaves the inverted coefficient square.
Injectivity of the adjunction Hom equivalence proves the equality, with the two object isomorphisms already constructed.

mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits including mateEquiv_counit, conjugateEquiv_counit, and conjugateEquiv_comm in Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Mates. They describe one mates correspondence; the required objectwise square also combines two changes of adjunction and a unit arrow. Proved the combination using the existing uniqueness counit API.
One exact API hit in Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Unique; used for the two representing-object isomorphisms.
Eleven hits, including rightAdjointUniq_hom_app_counit and its natural-transformation form, plus uses in locally Cartesian closed categories. No exact two-coefficient-square statement.

theorem counitMates_transport
    {C D C' D' : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] [Category C'] [Category D']
    {LO LC : C ⥤ D} {RO RC : D ⥤ C}
    {LO' LC' : C' ⥤ D'} {RO' RC' : D' ⥤ C'}
    (aO : LO ⊣ RO) (aC : LC ⊣ RC) (bO : LO' ⊣ RO') (bC : LC' ⊣ RC')
    (Q : C ⥤ C') (T : D ⥤ D')
    (tA : LO ≅ LC) (tB : LO' ≅ LC')
    (qO : LO ⋙ T ≅ Q ⋙ LO') (qC : LC ⋙ T ≅ Q ⋙ LC')
    (K : D) (K' : D') (unit : T.obj K ⟶ K')
    (uO : Q.obj (RO.obj K) ⟶ RO'.obj K')
    (uC : Q.obj (RC.obj K) ⟶ RC'.obj K')
    (hO : LO'.map uO ≫ bO.counit.app K' =
      qO.inv.app (RO.obj K) ≫ T.map (aO.counit.app K) ≫ unit)
    (hC : LC'.map uC ≫ bC.counit.app K' =
      qC.inv.app (RC.obj K) ≫ T.map (aC.counit.app K) ≫ unit)
    (hc : T.map (tA.hom.app (RO.obj K)) ≫ qC.hom.app (RO.obj K) =
      qO.hom.app (RO.obj K) ≫ tB.hom.app (Q.obj (RO.obj K))) :
    ∃ (eA : RO.obj K ≅ RC.obj K) (eB : RO'.obj K' ≅ RC'.obj K'),
      Q.map eA.hom ≫ uC = uO ≫ eB.hom
